agent.problem: Judah has not appeared in any earlier card, and the setup gives no clue from which the baker can reason out the kingdom's name. The blank therefore tests unseen wording rather than meaning the baker can work out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: No card mentions that the people also poured out drink offerings to other gods on these rooftops. Since this card asks what the people did there, covering only the incense leaves out part of the very conduct for which the houses would be defiled in verse 13.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

human.problem: Stop 1 card 12 and stop 2 card 2 build their content on Jeremiah 18, the previous passage. The docs say that passage is provided 'for context only. It is not part of the lesson,' but they also allow facts from outside the passage when they help, with a reference.
human.question: May Prep cards quote or call back to the previous passage (here, Jeremiah 18:4 and 18:12) to set up a contrast or question, or should the previous passage be used only as background for the writer and never appear on a card?
